identity: Literary Arabic prose fiction: a continuous chapter-run from Abbas Mahmoud al-Aqqad's novel Sara (characters Hammam, Sara, Zahir, Mariana). Third-person psychological narration in ornate early-20th-century MSA, interleaved with two embedded registers: (a) an imagined one-woman play script in which the speaker label sara stands alone on its own line and the turn follows it, and (b) reported conversation introduced by quotative frames (qala / qalat / fa-sa-alaha / qa-ilan). Toward the end the narration slips into free indirect discourse (madha yaqul / a-tastasghiruni / la wallahi), rendered as a staccato run of very short lines.
law: The unit is the orthographic period-unit, and in this corpus it is SHORT: 1483 content tokens over 117 NL-delimited lines, mean 12.7 tokens. The line structure here is finer than paragraph-level - the source breaks at essentially every terminal stop, so one-token lines (a-tastasghiruni), two-token lines (ya lil-ar, la wallahi), and even an interrupted turn ending on a dangling wa (daawtu sara wa) each occupy a line of their own. The decisive consequence: material that SHARES a line is presumptively ONE sentence, comma-chained. This corpus is a precision trap, not a recall trap. Al-Aqqad chains freely with wa- and fa-, and the line-initial tokens of this very document are overwhelmingly wa-/fa-initial (wa-kana, wa-khatara, wa-lam, wa-alfa, fa-dalafa, fa-raddat, fa-nazarat, fa-ahabba, fa-nasiyat), which proves wa-/fa- is not evidence in either direction and must never by itself license a split. Negation correlatives (lam takun ... innama; lam yaqsid ... wa-innama), relatives (allati / alladhi), hatta, raythama, kama, conditional in, and coordinated imperatives are sub-sentential and never break. A quotative frame and the speech it introduces take a colon, never a period, and stay inside one sentence. I therefore posit an unmarked internal boundary ONLY where a line falls far outside the corpus length envelope AND carries a seam no comma could plausibly bear. The length distribution supplies exactly that test: line lengths run 1 to 47 with a clean gap, then two outliers of 84 and 85 tokens - 1.8x the next longest and 6.6x the mean. Those two lines, and only those, take internal boundaries.
reasoning: FRAMEWORK FIRST. I had to settle whether NL marks every sentence (which would make the task vacuous) or only the source's line layout. Line 187-189 ends on a bare dangling conjunction wa (daawtu sara wa, an interrupted turn), and no sentence can end on a conjunction - so NL is layout, not punctuation, and unmarked internal boundaries must exist somewhere. But the 12.7-token mean and the abundance of 1-2 token lines show that layout tracks sentences very closely, so those boundaries are rare. I used the length distribution as the discriminator (1..47, gap, 84, 85) and admitted splits only inside the two outliers. SITE 698-782 (85 tokens), boundary at 706 malama. This is the strongest single piece of evidence in the document. All sixteen other quotations here are line-final: qala hammam ... ayna zahir ya madam; wa-qalat awwalan narak illa za-iran li-zahir; qa-ilan ara anna al-dika al-yawm italiyya; fa-sa-ala al-kha-ita a-hadha dayf jadid; fa-hazzat ra-saha ... awfaruha nasiban fi al-mirath. This line alone puts the quote FIRST (hadd-i min raw-ik, innama thana-un aradtu la malama) and then resumes narration with a finite verb, wa-akhadha yashrah laha. A 16/16 regularity broken exactly once is best explained by a period at malama that the line break failed to record. I considered and rejected reading qala ... wa-akhadha as two coordinated verbs of one subject in one sentence: the intervening direct speech would have to be closed off first. I did NOT split at 768 dahika (the frame introducing the closing joke - colon, not period) nor at 770 rabbak (ihmad rabbak, indaka min sara ... is the same interjection-plus-comma shape this corpus keeps on one line elsewhere). SITE 549-632 (84 tokens). I rejected a break at 564 malamiha, because lam takun ... innama is a bound negation-correction correlative and one sentence. I took 603 al-wada as the sharpest seam: the text leaves Sara's particular face and turns to a gnomic maxim about women in general (wa-tilka sinaatun tahdhaquha kullu imra-atin taltafitu ila mahasiniha), a specific-to-generic shift a comma carries poorly. I added 619 mir-aha at LOW confidence, before the contrastive pivot lakinnaha lam takun taltafit ila ma wara-a dhalik, which completes the paragraph's argument (she had mastered the surface, not the depths); the counter-evidence is that wa-lakin occurs mid-line three times in this document and never line-initially, making lakin a weak boundary cue here - hence lo. If the line takes only one period, 603 is my bet; I list both because 84 tokens is far too long for a single period. REJECTED SITES, each argued and dropped under the shares-a-line-means-one-sentence rule. 541 kifaya (qala hammam kifaya | laqad zafirna bi-tasfiq al-mumaththila): genuinely tempting, because laqad opens a line in four of the five places it occurs in this document and this is its only mid-line occurrence; but the whole line is just 9 tokens, already sentence-sized, and kifaya + comma + laqad zafirna is an ordinary interjection. 477 wal-hayya (hadha kalam al-ajaiz / hadha hadith khurafa / hadha madhhab atiq | innama khuliqna lil-surur): the asyndetic tricolon is comma anaphora, and decisively, this corpus gave the two-token outburst ya lil-ar its own line one step earlier - had these been separate sentences they would have been separate lines too. 56 fiha: tadur muhawaratuha ala al-mithal al-ati is the tail that introduces the script with a colon. 114 thiyab, 152 taruquha, 299 sadiqati, 435 al-gharam, 798 bidayatiha, 1115 al-sabah, 1423 al-maqam, and the wa-anzuri of 1494-1539: all comma-level fa-/wa- appendages inside lines already within the length envelope. I also walked every line of 33-47 tokens (880-926, 1494-1539, 0-41, 838-878, 979-1018, 1155-1191, 634-669, 1193-1227, 1429-1461, 1036-1068) and each proved a single coherent Aqqadian period built on one main clause plus relatives and coordinated verbs, with no seam a period could occupy. Final count: 117 line-mandated boundaries plus 3 posited internal ones = 120.
